title: When the Python SDK ends a ZIA session and what that does to staged changes

prose.text: This is about when the Python SDK ends a ZIA session and what the platform then does with staged changes. The platform behavior is documented by the provider guide, and the SDK only decides when the session ends.

prose.label: What the platform does.
prose.text: {{exit-can-activate}} The platform behavior it rests on is [[zia.terraform.activation-methods:session-end-autoactivation]]. The same behavior seen from a time-interval write is in [[zia.time-intervals.api-surface]].

checks.do: Whether the script wrote anything before it exited, and which client type it used, when asked whether changes went live without an activate call.
Whether the tenant has been migrated to Zidentity before relying on the admin-role or admin-user calls.

oneapi-exit-deauthenticates.statement: Leaving a `ZscalerClient` `with` block on the OneAPI client calls the executor's `deauthenticate` for a ZIA or ZTW session; for ZIA the code comment says it deauthenticates only if mutations occurred.

quotes: # For ZIA, deauthenticate only if mutations occurred; executor will decide.
if service_type.lower() in ["zia", "ztw"]: # For ZIA, deauthenticate only if mutations occurred; executor will decide.

deauth-only-after-mutation.statement: The executor marks a session as mutated on any POST, PUT or DELETE, and skips the ZIA logout when none occurred; the code comment says ZIA requires the explicit logout to activate staged configurations.

quotes: if service_type.lower() in ["zia", "ztw"] and not self._mutations_occurred:
Both ZIA and ZTW require explicit deauthentication to activate staged configurations

legacy-exit-always-logs-out.statement: The legacy ZIA client's context exit always calls `deauthenticate()`, which sends a DELETE to `/api/v1/authenticatedSession` and treats only a 204 as success; it does not check for earlier writes.

quotes: def __exit__(self, exc_type: Optional[type], exc_val: Optional[Exception], exc_tb: Optional[Any]) -> None: logger.debug("deauthenticating...") self.deauthenticate()
self.auth_details = None return True else: return False

exit-can-activate.statement: A Python script that writes through a `with` client and then exits the block ends its ZIA API session, so the platform activates its pending changes without an explicit activate call. A script that only reads does not trigger that logout.
exit-can-activate.conditions: Holds when the logout DELETE succeeds (OneAPI `deauthenticate` treats only HTTP 200 as success and otherwise only logs a warning), for the OneAPI client with ZIA as the last service used; the legacy client logs out on every exit, so its with block ends the session whether or not it wrote.

password-expiry-zidentity.statement: The Python docstrings for the admin-role password-expiry get and update calls say the method is not compatible with Zidentity-enabled tenants, and the admin-user list docstring says the endpoint returns an empty list for tenants migrated to Zidentity.

quotes: Note: This method is not compatible with Zidentity enabled Tenants
Note: This method is not compatible with Zidentity enabled Tenants
For tenants migrated to Zidentity this endpoint will return an empty list.

password-expiry-endpoint.statement: The current Python `update_password_expiry_settings` sends its PUT to `/passwordExpiry/settings`.
